about: Robinhood Chain MAINNET (4663). NOT READY TO DEPLOY: the script refuses this file while the word T-O-D-O appears anywhere in it, and it appears beside every value a person has not confirmed. Confirmed by a person (Thom, 2026-10-12): timelock.owner, the Safe, and the guardian. Also confirmed by him that day: SPY's pool, and that GLD is listed. Not confirmed: every other asset's pool, every asset's ceiling (maxWeightBps) and largest trade (maxTradeUsd), the bound to the feed (priceBoundBps), the rail and the average pools for a stale feed (staleRailBps, average), and the eight tokens added on 2026-10-12. The first mainnet step is owner-signed vaults only: no keeper (keeperEnabled false, keeper zero, every asset's flags 0), so no averageFeed is needed yet; the pool-average feed fills that slot when the keeper comes. The admin and the beacon's owner is a TimelockController the script creates; timelock.owner is the Safe that proposes to it. Listed: USDG as cash and nine tokens (NVDA, SPY, AAPL, MSFT, GOOGL, AMZN, META, TSLA, GLD), each with its Chainlink feed and its feedDescription, and each with `pool`: the one hookless Uniswap v4 pool against USDG its trades go through (fee in hundredths of a basis point, tick spacing). Each also states `maxTradeUsd`, the largest single trade the app builds. The deploy script reads `priceBoundBps` and `maxTradeUsd` only to refuse a file that leaves one out, and reads neither `pool`, `staleRailBps` nor `average` (the contracts hold no pool and check an owner's swap against its minimum only); the app's builder and, for the pool, the guard do, and test/fork/RobinhoodForkDeploy.t.sol trades every listed token through it on a fork. All read at block 86735800 on 2026-10-12 by packages/chain-evm/test/pool-quotes.ts (ROBINHOOD-MAINNET-SCOPE, section of that day). Not listed: QQQ and SGOV, whose v4 pools against USDG do not fill a $1,000 trade. No deposit cap is set (caps none; Thom, 2026-10-10): the per-vault and total caps exist in the contracts and the Safe can set them later through the timelock. Closed days are the NYSE closures the test network file carries. safeMinThreshold is the fewest signatures the Safe must need (2 at least on a mainnet). Anyone may create a vault; naming creators would restrict it to them.

timelock.ownerNote: The Safe Thom created on Robinhood Chain on 2026-10-12 (block 86,734,497). Read on chain that day: Safe 1.5.0, threshold 2, owners 0x0a1c3312c808b23D019bF241028f6B5624f4cc98 (Thom Gabriel) and 0xAC3cBBCd6e51dBFAf4e79d5E8Cf54a1622D71e0e (Rodrigo Trindade), no module enabled, no guard, nonce 0. Recorded in docs/vault/SECURITY.md. With two owners and a threshold of two, one lost key locks it.

guardianNote: Thom Gabriel's address, confirmed by Thom on 2026-10-12. It can only pause. It is also one of the Safe's two owners, by his decision (docs/vault/SECURITY.md). Never the deployer, never the keeper's machine.
sessionPriceAgeNote: TODO: a person confirms the second use of this value. For the contracts it is how fresh a price must be for the keeper in session. The app also reads it from the deploy record as how young a feed's answer is while the feed itself is the witness of an owner's trade: an hour. Older than that, a token whose `average` is usable is held to its pool's last hour instead (inside staleRailBps of the feed's last answer), so an honest move overnight or over a weekend is not refused against a price from the last close; a token whose `average` is not usable keeps the feed up to its maxAge.
priceBoundNote: TODO: a person confirms the bound. How far a pool's quote for an owner's trade may be from the token's Chainlink price, pool fee included, before the app refuses to build the trade: 2%, the bound test/fork/RobinhoodForkDeploy.t.sol holds every listed token's fill to (MAX_COST_BPS). Source: the listed pools cost 0.01% to 0.97% at their largest trade and sat at most 0.35% from their feeds at block 86735800, so 2% leaves room for a moving market and refuses a pushed pool. The deploy script does not read it (the contract checks an owner's swap against its minimum only); the app's builder does, from the deploy record, and never sets a minimum under the feed's price less this bound.
staleRailNote: TODO: a person confirms the rail. While a token's Chainlink feed is older than its maxAge (a stock's, from Saturday evening to Sunday evening), the app checks an owner's trade against the last hour's average price of the token's `average` pool instead, by the same priceBoundBps, and refuses outright when the pool's quote is more than this far from the feed's last answer, however old: 10%. Proposed by Thom's direction of 2026-10-12 (gate OWNER-PRICE-BOUND). The deploy script does not read it.
